---
title: "Exponent after an open ball"
format:
  pdf:
    include-in-header:
      - ../macros-pdf-header.tex
      - ../macros.qmd
---

An exponent after an open ball must rise over a tall argument,
and the radius must print as a subscript of the ball symbol.

```{=latex}
\newsavebox{\withexp}\newsavebox{\withoutexp}
\sbox{\withexp}{$\ball{\frac{a}{b}}{r}^2$}
\sbox{\withoutexp}{$\ball{\frac{a}{b}}{r}$}
\par\ifdim\dimexpr\ht\withexp-\ht\withoutexp\relax>1.5pt BALLEXPRISES\else BALLEXPSTUCK\fi
\sbox{\withexp}{$\ball{\vx}{\tolin}$}
\sbox{\withoutexp}{$B\paren{\vx}$}
\par\ifdim\dimexpr\wd\withexp-\wd\withoutexp\relax>1pt BALLRADIUSPRINTED\else BALLRADIUSMISSING\fi
```

The radius check compares widths, because the parenthesis already reaches
as far below the baseline as the subscript does.
A body without the radius is its control, and must come out missing.

```{=latex}
\newcommand{\noradiuscontrol}[2]{{B\paren{#1}}}
\sbox{\withexp}{$\noradiuscontrol{\vx}{\tolin}$}
\sbox{\withoutexp}{$B\paren{\vx}$}
\par\ifdim\dimexpr\wd\withexp-\wd\withoutexp\relax>1pt RADIUSCTRLPRINTED\else RADIUSCTRLMISSING\fi
```

The rejected form is the control: an unbraced body must not rise, so the test can fail.

```{=latex}
\newcommand{\unbracedcontrol}[2]{B_{#2}\paren{#1}}
\sbox{\withexp}{$\unbracedcontrol{\frac{a}{b}}{r}^2$}
\sbox{\withoutexp}{$\unbracedcontrol{\frac{a}{b}}{r}$}
\par\ifdim\dimexpr\ht\withexp-\ht\withoutexp\relax>1.5pt CTRLRISES\else CTRLSTUCK\fi
```
